strengths: Well-motivated core insight with elegant intuition (Figure 1): smooth aggregate loss masks multiple simultaneous phase transitions that become visible in directional decompositions
Strong synthetic validation: recovering 'carrying' skill (homogeneity 0.973) in arithmetic task when exact loss fails (0.514) convincingly demonstrates the method's value

Sound technical approach: proper theoretical grounding with Hessian-based basis construction, second-order Taylor approximation with clear derivations, and justification from linear mode connectivity literature
Thorough experimental rigor: comprehensive ablations (decomposition strategy, basis choice, first vs. second-order) showing POLCA substantially outperforms alternatives
Interpretable results on natural language: discovered clusters correspond to meaningful grammatical constructions (appositive phrases, etc.) validated through POS analysis and context inspection
Clear presentation and good reproducibility: well-written with clear figures, detailed hyperparameters, and principled algorithm descriptions
weaknesses: Critical scalability limitation: experiments only on small models (9M and 40M parameters) with coarse checkpoint intervals (200-750 iterations). For a paper about 'language model training,' inability to scale Hessian eigendecomposition to modern LLMs significantly limits impact and relevance
Limited technical novelty: core contribution is relatively straightforward extension of LCA to arbitrary basis vectors and per-sample losses; incremental rather than transformative innovation

Weak theoretical justification for basis choice: key assumption that datapoint Hessians share eigenvectors with aggregate Hessian is acknowledged as 'unlikely correct'; Appendix E shows random bases achieve ~90% vs 97% homogeneity, undermining claims about Hessian eigenvector interpretability

Insufficient validation of natural language results: (1) no quantitative cluster quality metrics unlike arithmetic task, (2) cluster labeling semi-automated relying on manual context inspection, (3) unclear if discovered patterns are novel insights vs. recovering well-known linguistic phenomena, (4) no sensitivity analysis for HDBSCAN hyperparameters

Second-order approximation concerns: Equation 6 relies on potentially unstable ratios and assumptions acknowledged to be incorrect; justification is primarily empirical (Appendix F) rather than theoretical
Limited evaluation scope: only two task domains (synthetic arithmetic and Wikipedia); more diverse tasks needed to validate generality of the approach
